title: A Crown for the Oath
premise: Wren Galloway has spent a decade keeping the Hollowgate sealed and the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, a quiet brotherhood that trades in impossible things, hidden from a crown that fears magic. When King Aldric's witch-hunters burn the guildhouse and seize its ledger of names, Wren flees with the one page that matters: the original covenant between the human realm and the fading Otherworld, which only a gatekeeper's blood can reforge. Hunted by the inquisitor Serah Vane—who is herself hiding the gift—Wren gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced knight, a child who speaks to doors, and a smuggler who once betrayed them. At the ruined Hollowgate on midwinter night, Wren learns the covenant demands a keeper's life as its hinge; instead they offer their name and memory, erasing themselves from every ledger and mind but sealing both realms in balance. The book ends with Wren unknown even to those who love them, walking through a world where the gift is no longer hunted—and a single blank page waiting for whoever remembers them first.
about_author: Gideon Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing sealed municipal records before turning to fiction. They write about gates, ledgers, and the people history forgets on purpose.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Doors
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine night at the Hollowgate: Wren checks wards, balances the Guild's impossible ledger, and shares supper with old Keeper Bram. The emotional beat is quiet contentment shadowed by dread—the wards have been humming wrong for weeks, and Bram refuses to say why.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Royal criers announce the Gift-Hunt: all bearers of the gift must register or burn. Wren watches neighbors denounce each other and realizes the Guild's anonymity is a countdown, not a shield. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Bram reveals the covenant-page hidden in the ledger and confesses Wren was chosen as keeper because their blood opens the Hollowgate. Before he can explain more, witch-hunter lanterns crest the hill. Beat: betrayal of safety, inheritance of burden.

chapters.title: What Burns in the Night
chapters.summary: Serah Vane's POV. The inquisitor leads the raid on the guildhouse, hunting the stolen page. She feels the gift stir in herself as she watches Bram die, and hides it. Beat: her certainty begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Road Out of Ellsmere
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fleeing with the page and Bram's iron key, Wren is ambushed by bounty men and saved by Dame Isolde Ferrant, a knight stripped of rank for refusing to hunt children. Beat: reluctant alliance, first taste of found family.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Talks to Doors
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. In a flooded quarry town they find Pip, an orphan whose gift opens any lock, imprisoned in a cage meant for witches. Isolde breaks her last oath to free him. Beat: choosing mercy over law.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Their escape route runs through Corvo Ashe, the smuggler whose testimony once cost Wren their family. He owes the Guild a debt and hates paying it. Beat: old wounds reopened; uneasy truce struck.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Unplaces
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip maps the shifting roads to the Otherworld's border while the group hides in Corvo's hold. His wonder softens the crew into something like kin. Beat: warmth before the storm; Wren almost believes they might make it.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Interrogating a captured Guild scribe, Serah realizes the crown isn't hunting the gift—it's harvesting it to force the Hollowgate open and drain the Otherworld. Beat: horror at complicity.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge at Greywater
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A checkpoint trap forces Wren to use their gatekeeper blood publicly to save Pip, exposing them. Serah, overseeing the bridge, lets them pass—and lies in her report for the first time. Beat: sacrifice, and an enemy turned uncertain.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Vellum Guild
chapters.summary: Corvo's POV. The group returns to the burned guildhouse seeking the second half of the covenant rite and finds survivors instead: apprentices hiding in the cellar vaults. Beat: grief transmuted into responsibility; the family grows.

chapters.title: The King's Empty Crown
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. At court she discovers King Aldric is dying, sustained by stolen gift-energy, and the hunt is his life-support. She steals the rite's missing fragment and deserts. Beat: treason born of conscience.

chapters.title: Hunted Together
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Serah catches up to the fugitives; knives are drawn until Pip vouches for her. Wren cannot forgive what she did to Bram. Beat: friction inside the found family; trust tested and grudgingly given.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the Hollowgate's outer shrine, the door itself shows Wren visions: every keeper before them, and the truth that the covenant's price is a keeper's life. Beat: despair; Wren conceals the price from the others.

chapters.title: The Long Midwinter March
chapters.summary: Corvo's POV. The company crosses frozen wilds pursued by the king's remaining hunters. Corvo, dying of an old wound, teaches Wren everything he knows about sacrifice disguised as trade. Beat: mortality, mentorship, love confessed sideways.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. A sheltering shepherd sells them out for the bounty. In the fight, Corvo dies holding the pass so the others can run. Beat: devastating loss; the family bound tighter by grief.

chapters.title: The Price on the Page
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Reading the complete rite, Serah learns the covenant's true cost and confronts Wren, who admits they planned to die alone at midnight. The group refuses to allow it. Beat: anger as love; the theme of justice outside the law made explicit—they will rewrite the covenant itself.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Hollowgate
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The king's host arrives as the group begins the rite; Isolde holds the causeway, Pip unseals the inner door, Serah turns her own hunters' fire aside. Beat: chaos, courage, every thread converging.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the threshold, Wren attempts self-sacrifice—but the covenant accepts any keeper's freely offered name, not their life. Wren speaks their name into the gate, trading memory and identity for renewal. Beat: climax; transcendence through surrender rather than death.

chapters.title: The Balance Reforged
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The gate seals whole; the Otherworld's gift flows back into the land, breaking the king's stolen power. Aldric falls; Serah stands before the army and tells the truth. Beat: catharsis; the hunt ends not by decree but by witness.

chapters.title: Ledgers Left Blank
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Aftermath: the survivors rebuild the Guild openly, with Serah as its advocate. But none of them can remember Wren's face—only a shape of gratitude and a blank ledger page. Beat: bittersweet mourning for someone still alive.

chapters.title: The First Page
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, unnamed. A stranger with no past arrives at a rebuilt gate and finds a fresh ledger, a warm hearth, and four people who feel they've known them forever. Pip hands them a pen. Beat: hope; identity reborn through found family, the story closing where it began—at a door.
